note: Bank wording that describes HOW money moved, so it can be removed to leave WHO it moved to. Keyed by parser profile, with a generic set that always applies. Bank detection already covers FNB, Standard Bank, ABSA, Nedbank, Capitec, Investec and unknown; the counterparty layer has to cover the same ground or an FNB statement manufactures a counterparty called FNB.
why_self_reference_matters: The issuing bank prints its own name on its own transactions: 'FNB App Payment To Mr D Food' is a payment to Mr D Food, not to FNB. Left in, every workspace on that bank grows a counterparty named after its own bank, and unrelated payments group under it. But the name may only be stripped when it IS the issuing bank — on the real Standard Bank statement, six monthly payments of R19,086.55 go TO ABSA BANK, and ABSA is a genuine counterparty there. So self-reference is resolved from the run's detected bank, never from a list of bank names.
provenance: The fnb_business_v1 and standard_bank_business_v1 entries are transcribed from real statements processed by this system. The other profiles carry no bank-specific wording yet because no real statement from them has been seen — inventing plausible phrasing would be guessing, and the generic set plus self-reference stripping already covers them safely. Add wording here when a real statement provides it.

residual_noise_note: What may be left over after the channel wording and the issuing bank's name are removed, and which identifies nobody on its own. Stripping ABSA from 'ABSA BANK 8090806375 ACCOUNT PAYMENT' on an ABSA statement leaves 'BANK' — a counterparty called Bank is worse than no counterparty, because it groups unrelated rows under a name that means nothing. When nothing but these words remains, the honest answer is None.
